Embedded Software Engineer (m/f/d)

data.description:
Your mission

Your mission is to design and maintain a scalable, asynchronous backend that powers OKAPI:Orbits' end-to-end solutions across mission design, Space Situational Awareness (SSA), Space Traffic Management (STM), Flight Dynamics (FD), and Space Traffic Coordination (STC), supporting satellite operators throughout their entire mission lifecycle.

You'll work primarily on external customer projects with a Python-based tech stack, while also contributing in parallel to our products built on Java Spring Boot. You design and implement robust microservices that process and distribute large volumes of orbital and telemetry data to deliver reliable APIs and automation processes. You already bring solid experience and take independent ownership of parts of the backend architecture across both environments.

You'll work on the systems that enable satellite operators and space agencies to analyze, coordinate, and protect their missions in an increasingly crowded space environment.

Studies show that women are less likely to apply for a position if they don't meet 100% of the requirements. Please know that we explicitly encourage you to apply if this applies to you, as long as you bring a passion for space technology, reliable software development, and sustainable use of space.
OKAPI:Orbits already brings together a highly diverse team and is actively committed to growing that diversity further, since studies show that heterogeneous teams achieve better results and drive innovation.


Your tasks and responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain asynchronous, microservice-based backend systems, primarily in Python for external customer projects and in parallel in Java Spring Boot for our products
  • Implement and optimize data processing and distribution pipelines that handle large volumes of orbital, telemetry, and mission data
  • Design and maintain message-based communication structures between microservices (e.g., via RabbitMQ or comparable message brokers)
  • Collaborate closely with space engineers and scientists to translate mission-related requirements into scalable, robust software solutions
  • Share responsibility for the backend architecture across both tech stacks, with a focus on performance, fault tolerance, and maintainability
  • Plan and document implementation steps, from system architecture through deployment in a cloud-native environment
  • Ensure code quality, automated testing, and adherence to security and development standards
  • Advance CI/CD pipelines, observability, and automation to support stable, continuous releases
  • Analyze and resolve complex issues in distributed systems with a focus on efficiency and reliability
  • Work within small, interdisciplinary teams, contributing your backend expertise to cross-functional projects


Your profile

Must-haves

  • Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or completed vocational training as a Fachinformatiker (IT specialist)
  • At least 2 years of professional experience with Python for backend development, scripting, automation, or data processing
  • At least 2 years of professional experience in backend software development with Java (Spring Boot or comparable)
  • Solid understanding of microservice architectures, asynchronous systems, and distributed communication patterns
  • Practical experience with testing and code quality assurance
  • Experience with, or willingness to quickly get up to speed on, message-based communication between services (e.g., RabbitMQ or comparable message brokers) and containerization (Docker)
  • Ability to independently plan, implement, and review complex features in close collaboration with engineers and scientists
  • Proactive communication, structured way of working, and good written and spoken English
Nice-to-haves
  • Experience with orchestration, particularly Kubernetes
  • Experience with code reviews and adherence to coding standards
  • Solid understanding of software architecture principles, including modular structure, scalability, and maintainability
  • Experience with secure software development
  • Background in or interest in the space or aerospace sector


Why us?

  • Flat hierarchy, small teams, flexible working hours
  • Up to 30 days’ vacation & up to 30 days’ workation per year 
  • Early responsibility, influence on the technical direction
  • Training budget for your personal development
  • Career paths to support and promote your long-term development
  • Corporate benefits (brand discounts, travel discounts, concert tickets, etc.)
  • Free German language course
  • Bahncard (25 within Braunschweig, 50 outside) 
  • Bike leasing 
  • Company pension scheme 
  • Subsidy towards Hansefit / Wellpass membership 
  • Participation in space events and conferences to promote sustainable space travel

data.description:
TechQuartier

For 10 years, TechQuartier has been the place in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, where the right people come together through events, programs, and accelerator initiatives to drive innovative growth. As a key driver of innovation in Frankfurt’s financial center, TechQuartier connects FinTech and GreenTech startup founders with established companies in future-shaping fields such as AI, quantum computing, and finance.

TechQuartier has been part of the Federal Digital Hub Initiative (de:hub) since its start in 2017. In 2024, TechQuartier was officially recognized as the FinTech Hub Frankfurt within the de:hub network. TechQuartier is also the organizer and host of the IMPACT FESTIVAL in Frankfurt – Germanys largest B2B event for digital & sustainable transformation.

TechQuartier continues to advance the startup ecosystem in the Frankfurt Rhine-Main region and strengthens its role as a central innovation hotspot in Europe. 

If you’re interested in taking on responsibility in a dynamic environment, contributing your own ideas, and driving innovation together with us, you’ve come to the right place.
  
Join our team full-time starting from january 2027. We look forward to receiving your application.


Why this role truly makes an impact

The IMPACT FESTIVAL brings together companies, start-ups, investors, and innovators to drive digital and sustainable transformation forward. To make this happen, it takes strong partners and a diverse range of exhibitors.

As a (Senior) Sales Manager, you will play a key role in acquiring new exhibitors, sponsors, and partners for the IMPACT FESTIVAL. With your instinct for business opportunities and your strong closing skills, you will directly contribute to the festival’s growth and economic success. This role is not just about managing existing accounts, but about actively creating new opportunities, acquiring a high number of exhibitors, convincing partners, and consistently driving the sales process through to contract signing.


What you will drive forward with us

  • You are responsible for selling our exhibitor, trade fair, sponsorship, and partnership offerings, from identifying and approaching potential customers through negotiation to contract signing.
  • You build a sustainable sales pipeline by combining inbound leads with proactive outbound activities to acquire new customers.
  • You develop existing customer relationships, identify cross- and upselling opportunities, and build long-term partnerships.
  • Together with the team, you further develop our sales strategy and pricing structure and identify new market opportunities.
  • You confidently lead negotiations with decision-makers, with a strong focus on closing deals, and develop tailored offers.
  • You ensure a structured handover to the onboarding and account management process and support it as needed.
  • You manage and document your sales activities in our CRM (Pipedrive) and use the data gained to manage, analyze, and optimize the pipeline.
  • You work closely with the IMPACT FESTIVAL team and other relevant departments at TechQuartier, ensuring smooth coordination and collaboration.


What you bring to the table

  • You have several years of experience in B2B sales, ideally in the trade fair, conference, event, or sponsorship industry.
  • You have a proven track record in acquiring new customers and experience in successfully driving complex sales processes through to closing.
  • You have a strong understanding of customer needs and market potential and bring experience in developing, implementing, and optimizing sales strategies and pricing structures.
  • You are a strong communicator, approachable, and confident when interacting with a wide range of stakeholders. You communicate fluently in both German and English.
  • You have strong negotiation skills, take initiative, and work in a structured and goal-oriented manner, while keeping track of multiple sales processes running in parallel.
  • You are eager to learn and bring a hands-on mentality and a solution-oriented approach.
  • You are confident working with CRM systems; experience with Pipedrive is a plus.
  • You are passionate about sustainability, digitalization, and innovation.

Not required, but definitely helpful
  • You have experience working in a startup or coworking environment and are familiar with the dynamics of agile work cultures.


What awaits you with us

Team-Spirit: We are an open‑minded, dedicated, and international team that truly embraces innovation and entrepreneurship. To spark new and creative solutions, we value diverse opinions and perspectives.
Innovation Hub: You will work in a modern and inspiring environment at the heart of Frankfurt’s start‑up ecosystem. Through constant exchange with start‑ups, you’ll discover new trends and technologies, build valuable connections, and take part in numerous events at TechQuartier.

DEINE MISSION

Du bist eingeschriebene:r Student:in, auf der Suche nach einem Job mit Sinn und Kund:innenkontakt? Du hast Lust, Deine Hands-On Mentalität bei uns einzubringen und in einem dynamischen Umfeld zu agieren und zu lernen?

Dann bist Du bei uns richtig: Als Werkstudent:in Key Account Management (all genders) unterstützt Du für 15 bis 20 Stunden pro Woche das Key Account Management Team des deutschlandweit größten Mehrwegsystems bei der täglichen Arbeit in der Betreuung und Verwaltung von Key Accounts sowie in der Umsetzung von Partner-Roll-Outs. 

Deine Aufgaben sind:

  • Du übernimmst administrative und organisatorische Aufgaben im Onboarding-Prozess von Key Accounts.
  • Du stehst mit potentiellen und bestehenden Partnern in Kontakt, informierst sie über die Abläufe unseres RECUP-/ REBOWL-Mehrwegsystems und trägst damit maßgeblich zur Eindämmung der Einwegflut bei.
  • Du übernimmst eigenständig Verantwortung für die Datenpflege in Hubspot – pflegst Deine Pipeline und Aktivitäten und hast Deine Ziele selbständig im Blick
  • Du unterstützt im operativen Tagesgeschäft bei unseren großen Bestandspartnern.
  • Du begleitest die Optimierung und Automatisierung vorhandener Prozesse.


WAS DU MITBRINGST

  • Du studierst aktuell im Bereich BWL, Vertrieb oder in einem vergleichbaren Studiengang, bist noch mindestens 1 Jahr eingeschrieben und mindestens 15 Wochenstunden verfügbar.
  • Du bringst Interesse für Vertrieb und Kund:innenkontakt mit und hast bestenfalls schon erste Erfahrungen gesammelt (bspw. durch Promo-Jobs oder Ähnliches).
  • Du zeichnest Dich durch eine strukturierte, gewissenhafte und eigenständige Arbeitsweise aus.
  • Du hast Spaß an klaren, zielorientierten Abläufen und bringst eine Hands-On Mentalität mit.
  • Du hast Freude an Recherchetätigkeiten und der Pflege von Daten.
  • Du verfügst über fließende, verhandlungssichere Deutsch Kenntnisse (C2 Niveau) in Schrift und Sprache.
  • Und Du bringst mit, was uns ausmacht: Herzblut für die Sache, Miteinander und Team-Orientierung für eine gute Zusammenarbeit, Transparenz & Integrität in Deinem täglichen Tun sowie Kawumms für mutiges, engagiertes Handeln.
Nice to have:
  • CRM-Erfahrung: Du hast bereits mit einem der klassischen CRM-Tools gearbeitet (z.B. Hubspot).


WAS WIR BIETEN

Eine verantwortungsvolle und sinnstiftende Arbeit mit echtem Mehrwert für die Gesellschaft. Ein schnell wachsendes, dynamisches Unternehmen, das viel Entwicklungs- und Gestaltungsraum sowie flexible Arbeitsmodelle für Dich bietet. Viel Raum für selbstbestimmtes Arbeiten und Eigeninitiative. Ein persönliches, positives und professionelles Miteinander und eine offene Feedbackkultur, die es allen erlaubt, auch mal Fehler zu machen - denn das gehört dazu.  
 
Wo können wir noch besser werden?
Wir wollen diverser werden, weil wir daran glauben, dass wir unsere Vision nur durch Vielfalt erreichen und nur durch Vielfalt Innovation entstehen kann. Wir freuen uns daher über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit internationaler Geschichte, Menschen aller Geschlechtsidentitäten, aller Altersgruppen, People of Color sowie Menschen mit Behinderung oder chronischer Krankheit. 
 
Du willst mit uns Mehrweg-Geschichte schreiben?
Großartig! Dann schicke uns ein kurzes, knackiges Motivationsschreiben sowie einen Lebenslauf über das Bewerbungsformular. Für uns zählen Deine Kompetenzen, Deine Erfahrungen und vor allem, ob Du Dich mit unseren Werten und unserer Unternehmenskultur identifizieren kannst. Da auch wir nicht vollständig vor unconscious Biases gefeit sind, bitten wir Dich, kein Foto mitzuschicken.

data.description:
About KIRA

Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

KIRA builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Engineering Lead owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

 

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

 

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

 

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

  • Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

 

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

 

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

Quantum Motion is a fast-growing quantum computing scale-up based in London founded by internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University with over 40 years’ experience in developing qubits and quantum computing architectures. Bringing together state-of-the-art cryogenic facilities and an outstanding interdisciplinary team, we are developing quantum processors based on industrial-grade silicon chips, with the potential to radically transform computing power in areas such as materials modelling, medicine, artificial intelligence and more.


Our Team

Since 2021 our team has been listed every year in the “Top 100 Startups worth watching” in the EE Times, and our technology breakthroughs have been featured in The Telegraph, BBC and the New Statesman. Our founders are internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University who have pioneered the development of qubits and quantum computing architectures. About Stora

Stora is building the operating platform for modern self-storage businesses.

Our software helps operators manage bookings, payments, customers, facilities and day-to-day operations from one place, while automating much of the work that traditionally makes running a self-storage business unnecessarily complicated.

In just over five years, Stora has grown from an early-stage product into a platform used by more than 500 operators.

We’re a product-led, remote-first company with an experienced engineering team and ambitious plans for what comes next.

Now, as the engineering organisation grows, we’re hiring an Engineering Manager to make sure the way we lead, develop and support engineers grows with it.

The Role

This is a genuine people leadership role.

You’ll manage approximately 12 engineers working across three product teams, with the team expected to continue growing.

Each product team has a Tech Lead responsible for technical direction, alongside Product and Design. Your focus is different: the engineers themselves.

This isn’t a role for somebody looking to move away from engineering completely, though. You’ll need enough technical depth to understand the work, follow engineering discussions and ask good questions without needing to be the person making every technical decision.

You’ll work closely with our Head of Engineering and have support from People, but you’ll have meaningful autonomy to improve how engineering management works at Stora.

What Else You’ll Own

Engineering Management

  • Manage engineers across multiple product teams through regular, useful 1:1s, coaching and clear feedback.

  • Make expectations clear and help engineers understand what good performance looks like.

  • Identify performance issues early and handle difficult conversations properly when needed.

  • Support engineers in progressing from junior through senior and beyond.

  • Build strong relationships with engineers without creating unnecessary management overhead.

Performance & Progression

  • Own the engineering performance and progression approach.

  • Review and improve our existing career levels, expectations and review processes.

  • Make promotion and progression decisions that are consistent, evidence-based and understood by the team.

  • Create a culture where feedback happens throughout the year rather than being saved for formal reviews.

Hiring & Team Development

  • Own engineering hiring alongside the relevant Tech Leads and wider team.

  • Help define what we need before a search begins, assess candidates properly and maintain a high hiring bar.

  • Ensure new engineers have a structured and useful onboarding experience.

  • Think proactively about team composition, capability gaps and future hiring needs.

Team Health

  • Pay attention to engagement, retention, collaboration and emerging people issues across the engineering organisation.

  • Work with Tech Leads when team problems sit somewhere between technical delivery, behaviour and team dynamics.

  • Help maintain a strong remote engineering culture as Stora grows.

Technical Context

  • Stay close enough to the engineering work to understand what the team is solving and the environment they’re working within.

  • Be comfortable reading code, following pull requests and participating intelligently in technical conversations.

  • Partner with Tech Leads without competing with them for technical ownership.

What Success Looks Like

After your first year, we’d expect:

  • Engineers to have a clear understanding of what is expected of them and how they can progress.

  • Managers and engineers to be having better, more useful conversations about performance and development.

  • Performance issues to be addressed early rather than becoming surprises.

  • A progression framework that works for the engineering organisation Stora has become, not the company we were several years ago.

  • Stronger and more consistent hiring and onboarding.

  • The Head of Engineering spending less time acting as the default people manager for the entire engineering organisation.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager, rather than somebody taking their first step into management.

You’ll ideally have:

  • Previous experience directly managing software engineers across more than one team or product area.

  • A strong track record of developing engineers at different stages of their careers.

  • Hands-on experience managing performance, including difficult or underperformance situations.

  • Experience making promotion and progression decisions.

  • Experience running or improving engineering career frameworks, review cycles or progression processes.

  • Previous experience hiring software engineers and building effective interview processes.

  • An engineering background that allows you to understand code and contribute meaningfully to technical conversations.

  • The judgement to know when to get involved and when to leave technical decisions with the Tech Leads.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly in a remote environment.

  • A practical understanding of how AI tools are changing software engineering and experience using them in your own work.

Experience with Ruby or Rails would be useful, but it isn’t essential.

We’re much more interested in whether you can lead engineers well.

What This Role Isn’t

It’s worth being clear that this isn’t:

  • a Tech Lead role with some people management added on;

  • a delivery or project management position;

  • a Product Manager role;

  • a hands-on engineering role where you’ll spend most of your week writing production code;

  • a first Engineering Manager opportunity.

Technical leadership already exists within the product teams.

We’re hiring you because engineering management itself deserves dedicated ownership.

Our Technology

You won’t be expected to spend most of your time writing production code, but you should be comfortable working around our stack.

Backend: Rails, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, TimescaleDB

Frontend: Turbo, React, ViewComponents, Sass

Testing: Minitest, Playwright

Deployment: GitHub Actions, Heroku

Salary & Benefits

  • Salary: Highly competitive and depending on experience

  • Location: Fully remote within the UK or Ireland

  • Belfast office: Available for anyone who wants to use it

  • Private health insurance for you and your family

  • Company pension

  • 35 days’ annual leave inclusive of applicable public/statutory holidays, depending on location

  • Learning and development support

  • Share options

  • Work-from-home budget

Our Hiring Process

We’re reviewing applications as they arrive rather than waiting for a closing date.

If your experience looks like a strong match, we’ll explain the process clearly from the outset and move quickly.

Equal Opportunities at Stora

Stora is an equal opportunities employer.c

We want to build a workplace where people are treated fairly, with dignity and respect, and where different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued.

We welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religious belief or political opinion, or sexual orientation.

Recruitment and employment decisions are based on merit, competence and business need, and we promote equality of opportunity and fair participation in line with our responsibilities under Northern Ireland equality legislation.

If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

We are hiring a Portfolio Partner to own our client book. Our clients are the portfolio: every company raising on Pairs gets a dedicated partner who carries their raise week to week. That partner is you.

Pairs is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients.

The role

You support every company working with us through the life of their raise. You run the weekly calls, keep momentum honest, prepare founders for the investor meetings that matter, debrief what happened, and strategize on an ongoing basis. You also bring a book of your own. Five or more years of relationships with family offices, VCs, HNW investors, and institutional allocators, built and kept warm, now put to work for the companies you manage. This is not a fund seat and you will not manage money. You manage raises and the founders running them. Your hours go to judgment, relationships, and the conversations that keep a raise moving. You report directly to the two co-founders and hold the most client-facing seat in the company.

What you will own

  • A book of client companies: the weekly rhythm, the momentum, and the relationship, from onboarding through close.

  • Investor meetings end to end for your book: prepared before, debriefed after, feedback captured and delivered honestly.

  • Your own investor relationships, worked for the portfolio: the right company in front of the right allocator at the right moment.

  • Raise readiness across your book: narrative, materials, and data room, kept sharp.

  • Renewals earned through ownership: clients stay because the seat works.

You are a fit if you

  • Have 5 or more years across capital markets, private placements, brokerage, or investment management, with direct work on private financings.

  • Hold real, current relationships with family offices, HNW investors, or institutional allocators: when you call, the call gets taken.

  • Have carried companies or clients through a financing personally: the weekly grind, the stalls, and the closes.

  • Are fluent in deal mechanics: terms, structures, diligence, and what investors actually ask before they commit.

  • Deliver hard news straight and early, and stay steady when a founder is not.

  • Treat discretion as a reflex: financials, cap tables, terms, and names stay confidential, always.

What we offer

Fully remote. Your day overlaps with US Eastern time, since that is when your clients and their investors are live. Meetings across the company batch on Mondays and Thursdays; your client rhythm runs on its own cadence. A client-facing seat reporting directly to both co-founders, real ownership of the client book, and relationships that produce visible outcomes.

The Role:


As a Member of Technical Staff on the EMEA field team, you build on top of one of the largest inference platforms in the world. The work spans the stack: capabilities on top of inference and serving, tooling around fine-tuning and post-training of LLMs, and the product our region’s customers need that the core platform team will not take on. You are first and foremost an excellent software engineer; that is what we are testing for. You prefer building product to being customer-facing, and that is exactly right for this role, though you are welcome to join customer work when it interests you.

 

Treat this as a flexible role: a bucket for exceptional builders at different levels of experience rather than a fixed job spec. There is no specific seniority requirement; anywhere from 3 to 10 years of experience can fit.

 

What we value most is first principles thinking: reasoning about unfamiliar problems from the ground up rather than from playbooks. You will be evaluated on this directly in the interview process, and strength here can outweigh gaps elsewhere in your background.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Build: Design and ship product capabilities end to end, from ambiguous need to running in production.

  • Build on Inference: Create capabilities on top of the serving stack: routing, model controls, observability, and whatever a deployment turns out to need.

About us

Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production.

 

Trusted by Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline, and more. We're an ambitious team of 100+ working at the frontier of AI and have raised $60M in Series C funding from Wellington Management, CRV, Next47 and Y Combinator.

 

The role

We're hiring a Learning & Development Specialist in London to design and deliver how Encord teaches the specialist workforce behind its human data — the annotators producing work for frontier AI labs and physical AI companies, in domains such as medical imaging and robotics, and on data types we are running for the first time. How well that workforce is taught is the largest controllable driver of the quality we ship.

You will work at the point where a technical specification becomes something a non-specialist can execute correctly: converting dense, sometimes ambiguous annotation guidelines into instruction a distributed workforce absorbs in days rather than weeks, and into assessment that proves they have.

That teaching problem is a real one, and it is why we are hiring for learning-science expertise rather than for training delivery. The people you teach are capable adults, but they are not domain experts, they come from a wide range of educational backgrounds, and they are frequently working in their second language. Managing cognitive load, breaking a specification into modules that build on each other, leading with worked examples before independent practice, and testing for what actually predicts performance on the job — that craft is the role.

It is a hands-on role. You will design the material and you will stand up and teach it, and it is measured in operational terms: ramp time to competence, first-pass quality, and how much of the workforce is qualified for the work we are selling.


What you'll do

  • Turn a client specification and a set of annotation guidelines into teachable material within days of a project launch — modular, sequenced, and built on worked examples, edge-case libraries and annotated failure cases

  • Design against explicit learning-science principles rather than instinct — manage intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load, chunk a dense specification into modules that build, scaffold then fade support, and use spaced retrieval so what is taught in week one survives to week four

  • Run live training sessions yourself, remotely and to distributed cohorts, daily during a project ramp — and adjust in the room when a concept is not landing

  • Build criterion-referenced assessments that decide readiness rather than test recall, with pass thresholds set alongside the Quality Systems Lead — so that nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard

  • Design for a novice audience by default: no assumed prior knowledge, plain language, and material that works for someone reading in their second language

  • Build durable curricula for the domains we sell repeatedly — medical imaging, document AI, LLM evaluation and red-teaming, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — with progression into higher-skill, higher-rate work

  • Coach the Human Data Program Managers into better teachers: session formats, feedback technique, and observation against a standard, since much of the instruction is delivered by them rather than by you

  • Sit with annotators and watch where they get stuck, then redesign — most of what you need to know is visible in the first hour someone spends on a new task

  • Partner with Product on what belongs inside the Encord platform as guidance at the point of work rather than in a course nobody re-opens

  • Measure every programme against a before-and-after in quality and throughput terms, and retire the ones that do not move an operational number

 

Who we're looking for

  • Grounded in learning theory, and able to say which principle you are applying and why — cognitive load, the worked-example effect, scaffolding and fading, spaced and retrieval practice, criterion-referenced assessment

  • You teach as well as design. You will be in front of a cohort regularly and you are good at it, including when the room is not following you

  • You design for the learner in front of you rather than for someone like yourself — assumed prior knowledge is the most common way training fails here

  • Execution-oriented: a project launching next week needs material this week, and competence in days rather than a term

  • Analytically rigorous. You read quality data and can tell which failures are teachable and which are not, and you are happy being measured on operational metrics rather than completion rates and satisfaction scores

  • You work from a technical specification, and you are often the person who notices the guidelines contradict themselves

  • A clear writer and a strong cross-functional communicator. Most of the workforce you are teaching you will never meet in person

  • Entrepreneurial: this is the first dedicated learning hire here, and you will invent the system rather than inherit one

 

Experience requirements

  • A formal grounding in education, learning science or instructional design — a degree, postgraduate qualification, teaching qualification or equivalent professional training. This is a requirement for this role rather than a preference

  • 3–6 years of professional experience designing and delivering training in an operational environment —where training was measured against production outcomes

  • Demonstrable live facilitation to adult learners, remotely and at cohort scale, not only one-to-one coaching

  • You have built curriculum and assessment from scratch, including assessments that genuinely discriminate between competent and not

  • Experience teaching non-specialist adults, ideally across languages, geographies and levels of prior education

  • Multi-format authoring: written documentation, video, and interactive assessment

  • Comfortable working in data: enough fluency to evaluate your own programmes against quality and throughput reporting

  • Bonus: a classroom or vocational teaching background, or a language-teaching qualification such as CELTA or equivalent

  • Bonus: experience working with teams in India or comparable delivery geographies

  • Bonus: familiarity with annotation, evaluation or model-training workflows

 

Why Encord

  • Competitive salary, commission, and equity in a high-growth startup

  • Strong in-person culture — most of the team works from our London office 4+ days/week

  • 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays

  • Annual learning & development budget

  • Travel for customer visits, events, and conferences across the UK and Europe

  • Company lunches twice a week

  • Monthly socials & bi-annual team offsites

About us

The role

We're hiring a Quality Systems Lead to own how Encord measures the quality of the human data we deliver to frontier AI labs, physical AI companies and enterprise AI teams — the standard itself, the systems that evaluate against it, and the audit function that produces the ground truth behind both. Data quality is what our customers buy. As we scale across data types — image and video, document, medical, LLM evaluation, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — quality coverage cannot scale linearly with headcount. So this role has two halves that make each other work. You will build automated evaluation: model-assisted and LLM-based screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output. And you will build and run a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists in India, whose judgements become the labelled ground truth that trains and calibrates that automated layer. As coverage automates, the audit team moves up to the cases models can't judge and to generating gold sets for each new data type we take on. It is an unusual combination — engineering and consistent QC operations in one person — and it is the combination the job needs. You will also have an advantage your counterparts elsewhere in the industry don't: Encord owns the platform this work runs on, so the measurement you build can become native capability in the product rather than internal tooling.

 

What you'll do

  • Build automated dataset quality evaluation and root-cause detection — model-assisted and LLM-as-judge screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output

  • Hire, train, calibrate and manage a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists based in our India operation, held to inter-rater agreement and catch rate rather than volume audited

  • Turn audit output into labelled ground truth that trains and validates the automated layer, and manage the ratio of automated to manual coverage deliberately over time

  • Own the quality standard for every data type we deliver — written rubrics with worked edge cases, golden sets, and acceptance criteria agreed with the customer, alongside the Special Projects lead, before the first batch ships

  • Build scoring systems that rank annotator and reviewer performance and feed routing, staffing and offboarding decisions

  • Set the pass thresholds that certification gates on, so nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard

  • Report quality KPIs to leadership, and into the reporting our Special Projects leads take to customers: accuracy against client spec, inter-annotator agreement, rework rate, cost of rework, and coverage

  • Work with Project Management on remediation — you produce the measurement and the diagnosis, production owns fixing the project, and the standard stays independent of the people being measured

  • Own the unit economics of quality: cost per audited unit, and the coverage you buy per pound spent

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to bring quality measurement into Encord platform as native capability

Who we're looking for

  • You build and you operate. You'll write the evaluation pipeline, and you'll also run the weekly calibration session with ten auditors in another country

  • Your instinct on a coverage problem is to automate it — you reach for a model, a heuristic or a better sampling design before you reach for more auditors

  • Statistically literate in a practical way: sampling design, agreement statistics, and the judgement to spot a metric being optimised against rather than met

  • You can hold a calibrated standard across a distributed team you don't sit with — you know that ten uncalibrated auditors produce ten standards

Ready to take the next step in your leadership career and make a real impact within a rapidly growing, patient-focused organisation?

We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Team Leader or Manager to join us as a Pharmacy Team Lead. This is an exciting opportunity to bring your leadership experience into a fast-paced healthcare environment, supporting, motivating and developing a high-performing team across both weekday and weekend shifts.

You do not need previous pharmacy experience or a pharmacy qualification for this role. What we are looking for is someone with strong people leadership experience who knows how to run a successful shift, manage competing priorities, support their team and maintain high standards in a busy operational environment.

As Pharmacy Team Lead, you will be right at the heart of our day-to-day pharmacy operations. This is a hands-on role where no two days will be the same. You will help coordinate shifts, manage changing priorities, resolve operational challenges and provide clear, confident guidance to colleagues.

You will act as a visible and approachable point of leadership on shift, ensuring workloads are managed effectively, standards are consistently maintained and any issues are identified and addressed quickly. You will also support the development of your colleagues through regular feedback, coaching and encouragement, helping them build their confidence, strengthen their skills and take pride in the service they provide.

Working closely with the Pharmacy Manager and wider Pharmacy Operations team, you will help drive continuous improvement across the pharmacy. Whether it’s finding better ways of working, improving efficiency, strengthening communication or supporting the implementation of new processes, you will have the opportunity to contribute ideas and make a genuine difference to how we operate.

This role would be perfect for someone who thrives in a busy environment, enjoys bringing people together and is ready to take greater ownership and responsibility. You will need to be organised, proactive and calm under pressure, with the confidence to make decisions, support colleagues and maintain excellent standards.

You don’t need to be a pharmacy expert — you need to be a great leader. We will support you in developing your understanding of our pharmacy environment, processes and requirements.

If you are an experienced Team Leader, Supervisor or Manager who is passionate about people, enjoys a fast-paced environment and is excited by the opportunity to build your knowledge within healthcare, we’d love to hear from you.

Fanvue is one of the fastest-growing creator monetisation platforms globally. We're an AI-powered, creator-first platform helping creators connect, engage, and earn directly from their audiences at scale. Following our recent Series A, Fanvue has surpassed $200M+ in annual recurring revenue, with triple-digit year-on-year growth, supporting hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans worldwide.

As Fanvue scales, we need to protect and grow revenue across our mid-to-long-tail creator base without relying on 1:1 CSM ratios. The Pooled CSM model is how we do that: one person owning a large book of creators through data-driven playbooks, automated workflows, and targeted interventions.

🎯 The Role

We're hiring a Pooled Creator Success Manager to own retention and revenue outcomes across a portfolio of 500+ creators in a 1:many, tech-touch model.

This is not a traditional CSM seat. You will not have a handful of named accounts and weekly check-ins. Instead, you will build and run scalable playbooks, monitor risk and contraction signals across a large cohort, and intervene where the data tells you to. Think CS operations meets account management.

You will report to Thea and work closely with the wider Creator Success team.

🚀 What You'll Do

  • Own a pooled book of 500+ creators with full accountability for gross revenue retention

  • Build, maintain, and iterate playbooks that drive retention, reduce contraction, and surface expansion opportunities at scale

  • Monitor creator health signals (engagement drops, earnings decline, support ticket spikes) and run targeted interventions before churn materialises

  • Run a weekly cadence: risk alerts, contraction monitoring, playbook execution reviews

  • Design and automate lifecycle touchpoints (onboarding sequences, re-engagement campaigns, feature adoption nudges) through CS platform workflows

  • Support the broader CS team by providing pooled coverage as more creators move out of dedicated 1:1 management

  • Provide reactive support to creators in the pooled segment when risks, problems, or support needs arise

  • Partner with Product, Support, Moderation, and Growth to close feedback loops and improve creator outcomes

  • Track and report on cohort-level retention, contraction, and engagement metrics

👀 Who You Are

  • Experienced in Customer Success, Account Management, or CS Operations, ideally in a tech-touch or SMB/scale segment

  • Hands-on experience with a CS platform (health scoring, playbook automation, lifecycle workflows)

  • Comfortable building playbooks, automations, and health scores from scratch, not just running someone else's

  • Data-literate: you can pull insights from dashboards, spot trends in cohort data, and translate them into actions

  • Strong written communicator who can craft clear, concise creator-facing messaging at scale

  • Comfortable managing a large book through systems and signals rather than personal relationships

  • Self-directed and structured, you set your own cadence and hold yourself accountable

  • Familiar with the creator economy, subscription platforms, or marketplace models (a plus, not a must)

✨ You'll Thrive Here If

  • You like building systems more than managing relationships one by one

  • You get energy from finding patterns in data and acting on them before anyone asks

  • You want ownership of a segment, not just a task list

  • You are motivated by retention metrics and commercial outcomes

⚠️ You'll Struggle Here If

  • You prefer deep 1:1 relationships over scaled models

  • You need someone else to build your workflows and tell you what to automate

  • You are uncomfortable with ambiguity or building processes from zero

  • You wait for problems to surface rather than hunting for them

🌍 Why Join Fanvue?

  • Sunday Times Best Places to Work, two years running. We don't just say we have great culture, we prove it

  • Fanvue supports hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans globally. The problems you solve here are real and immediate

  • AI-native engineering: we are not bolting AI on. It is core to our product and how we build

  • Series A momentum: triple-digit growth means the problems you solve today define the platform for years

  • Fully remote with unlimited PTO, flexible working hours, a London office and WeWork access when you want it

  • Salary reviews every six months, we don't wait for annual cycles to recognise your growth

  • Travel and office budgets for team off-sites or kitting out your home setup

  • Benefits package including gym memberships, apps, and more we're actively building out

⭐ Fanvue is for Everyone

We know that diverse teams build better products. Even if you do not meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. Potential, mindset, and ambition matter just as much as experience.

Introducing Neudata:

Neudata is the global leader in alternative and market data intelligence, helping investors, hedge funds and corporates discover, evaluate, and use data to make smarter decisions. Our independence is what really sets us apart - we provide objective, unbiased intelligence that our clients trust and depend on.

Our suite of products and services is built around client needs: Scout for alternative data sourcing and ESG insights, Ranger for traditional data intelligence, plus expert data monetisation consultancy and industry events. With offices in London, New York, and Shanghai and a team of 100 people, we combine global reach with a small-team culture where every individual can make an impact.

The Role:

We’re seeking an experienced Senior Research Consultant to join Neudata’s Research team and support our consulting clients by owning substantial pieces of each engagement – research, synthesis, coordination and client management. Sitting within Research and reporting to the Head of Research, this is a dedicated, hands-on role for someone who can own consulting projects end to end: scoping the work, structuring the analysis, writing the deliverables, and presenting the findings to clients directly.

This is a senior, client-facing role. You will regularly represent Neudata in front of senior stakeholders, handling detailed and unplanned questions as they arise, and producing polished, client-ready written analysis as a core part of the job. We’re looking for someone who can operate independently, exercise judgment, deal with ambiguity, and remain composed with demanding clients.

Your Key Responsibilities:

  • Own consulting engagements from kick-off through delivery, managing scope, timelines and quality, and acting as the day-to-day engagement lead for client communication and expectations

  • Structure project workstreams and personally produce the underlying analysis and written deliverables across data product strategy, pricing, go-to-market planning and buyer validation

  • Lead client meetings, working sessions and delivery readouts, fielding detailed questions from senior client stakeholders directly and translating complex data, market and technical input into clear, actionable recommendations

  • Plan and manage multiple concurrent engagements against agreed timelines and scope, proactively identifying and managing risks, dependencies and resourcing needs

  • Draw on the wider Research team for specialist input where useful, while owning the core deliverable and client-facing work end to end

  • Work closely with the Consulting practice on scoping, pricing input and follow-on opportunities, while reporting day to day within Research

  • Develop deep expertise in data monetisation, external data markets and buyer expectations, and contribute to internal frameworks, templates and client-facing insight

What You’ll Bring:

  • Proven, relevant experience in consulting, strategy, alternative data, analytics or a related advisory role - we're open on level of experience, from a few years' track record through to seasoned practitioners

  • Demonstrated project management experience, ideally leading complete engagements rather than individual workstreams

  • A confident, polished, client-facing operator, comfortable presenting to and fielding scrutiny from senior stakeholders independently

  • Strong written skills and a track record of personally producing, not just reviewing, high-quality client deliverables

Talent Acquisition Lead

📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 4 days WFH) | 💰 £60,000 - £70,000

Street Group is scaling fast toward an ambitious growth plan, and hiring is about to get harder: more senior roles, a higher bar, and a market where the best people don't apply; they get found and won. We need someone who owns how we hire, not just who we hire.

We're looking for a TA Specialist with a truly commercial mindset. Skilled at your craft - able to land the hardest hires yourself, but also understanding what will make a whole team better at hiring - from candidate attraction to relationship building; employer brand to candidate experience.

Why this role exists now

Our recruiting team is strong but stacked - and as we get busier, there’s no real capacity to ensure we’re constantly innovating and improving the mechanisms that let us hire quality people at pace. We’ve recently raised investment, and have ambitious goals to achieve - now is the time to fine-tune our recruiting engine so we can scale effectively over the next few years.

The role

This is a role of two halves. The first half is hands-on delivery. IC L5s at Street Group are expected to confidently own the hardest searches - senior roles, niche roles, brand new roles we’ve no experience hiring for. You’ll be expected to understand how the roles you’re hiring for tie in to commercial goals, what to prioritise and why. When you run into issues, you investigate, gather qualitative and quantitative data, conduct market research, and ultimately develop solutions to solve your own problems. You share your knowledge with the team in ways that bring them on the journey - not just the “what and how” but the strong “why” behind it.

The second half is taking our TA function from great to exceptional. Candidate experience, employer brand, AI, tooling, sourcing strategy, assessment - we do all of them well already, but our team holds ourselves to a high standard - and we want to do it all exceptionally well. You’ll collaborate with our Head of People on the most impactful initiatives to prioritise - the what, why, why now, and how it will be achieved and measured. We expect you to be passionate about TA; part of communities, intrigued by industry trends, new tools, best practices, and what other companies are nailing (and making sure we do it even better).

Growth opportunities

The business and People team will grow significantly over the next few years, and there is potential for this role to grow into a management role or specialise in a specific area, but the initial focus and goals will be hands-on, IC L5 work as mentioned above.

Who we're looking for

  • A senior recruiter with deep expertise across the full lifecycle, and the outside-in view: what the market's doing, what great TA teams do, and what it means for us.

  • Someone who holds themselves to a high standard - e.g. measuring their results against quality of hire rather than hires made.

  • Someone whose judgement colleagues calibrate against, trusted with delivering the most senior and confidential searches without a steer.

  • An AI-native mindset: you treat AI as leverage and are keen to learn from our team, and share what’s been working for you.

  • The credibility and communication skills to challenge a department head on a bad hiring decision, deliver hard market news to leadership, and come out with the relationship stronger.

  • Someone who makes the team better on purpose, not by accident: you share what you know and help develop the people around you.

Why you might not want to apply

We'd rather be honest up front, because this role won’t be for everyone.

  • If you want to move into people management now. This is a senior IC role. You'll coach, share knowledge, and set standards, but you won't have direct reports on day one, and you'll still be carrying reqs yourself. If a management title is what you're chasing now or in the imminent future, this isn’t the job for you.

  • If you're a brilliant solo recruiter but you don't have a history of lifting up the people around you. This role will impact how our entire TA function operates, and evidence of knowledge sharing from prior roles will be assessed during the interview process.

  • If AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. We love Claude Cowork, and have both built and used multiple other tools to improve and speed up our ways of working. We have a company-wide expectation that AI is utilised, so it will be a large part of this role.

  • If you tend to report the problems you’re facing in searches. We need someone who spots the funnel stage quietly losing good candidates, or the hiring plan the market won't support, and fixes it before anyone flags it. At IC L5, we don’t expect your manager to be the one flagging problems or coming up with solutions for you.

  • If you like to just crack on with recruitment. Connect with us and join the Talent MCR meetup - we’d love to connect - but this role will be expected to do more than just deliver.

If that list sounds like your kind of role, please apply and let us know why!

We recognise that women and people from underrepresented groups often apply for jobs only when they meet every single requirement listed. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application!

Who are Street Group?

We’re an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother and sister duo, Tom & Heather Staff. Most of us have personal experience of how painful moving can be, and Tom and Heather saw an opportunity to change this: utilising technology, as well as our incredibly talented team, to improve the industry for everyone.

Our products form a powerful duo, working harmoniously together to transform an agent’s job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK.

Back in 2015, our co-Founder, Tom Staff, spent his evenings building Spectre v1.0. He’d seen first-hand an opportunity to automate the very manual process of winning new business for estate agents. Spectre is now our multi-award-winning instruction generation tool, generating an average return on investment for them of over 3000%.

Street.co.uk then launched back in 2020 and serves as our game-changing CRM, allowing agents to deliver a service that aligns seamlessly with the modern, 'on-demand' needs of customers and their busy lifestyles.

Why join Street Group?

🏠 Hybrid-working - you can work from home up to 4 days per week
🏖️ Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!)
💪 Structured career growth and ongoing professional development
📚 £500 yearly L&D budget
🎂 Your birthday on us - we pay, you stay away
🙋 ‘Give something back’ - 2 paid days volunteering on us
👶 Enhanced maternity, paternity & adoption pay
🧠 Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured
🧘 Regular well-being initiatives
🚂 Public transport season ticket loans
🌷 Paid menopause leave
🌞 Holiday buying scheme
🚀 Joining a new team in an exciting business with huge ambition
👥 Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day
👩🏿‍💻 A chance to work on cutting-edge technology
🐶 Comfortable, relaxed office space - office dogs welcome!
🍻 Fully stocked fridge and beers (or an alternative) on us every Friday afternoon
🎊 Company and team off-sites, events and happy hours

🚗 Electric car salary sacrifice scheme
🌍 Feel good about sustainability - we're a climate-positive company!

Salary

£60,000 - £70,000, depending on experience. However, sometimes the perfect person is far more or less experienced than we anticipated. In these situations, planned ranges go out the window. If you think that might be the case, please apply and just let us know.


We care deeply about helping the tech industry become a more inclusive and diverse place, and we work hard to lead by example. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a complementary team of employees and building an inclusive environment for all. Candidates must be eligible to live and work in the UK and be able to perform the work specified.

 

Interview Process

3 stages = 60-minute video call with our Head of People > In-person interview with two members of the People team > Final interview with two members of our SLT.

We want to make our interviews as inclusive as possible, so if you need any adjustments made or if there's anything you think we should be aware of during the interview process, please do let us know.

 

A note on using AI in your job application

As a fast-moving and rapidly evolving tech company, we embrace the advantages of AI and encourage its use throughout our application process. However, our goal is to get to know and hire the authentic you - your skills, experience, and values. We don’t want to hire an AI-generated version of you. We consider AI to be a valuable tool, not something that should overshadow you as an individual.

How we use AI in the hiring process

Candidate experience is really important to us, and our Talent team use AI notetakers during interviews so they can focus purely on their conversation with you. All hiring decisions are made by humans - not AI. Let us know if you have any questions!

Job Description

Are you an experienced construction project leader with the commercial acumen to deliver complex infrastructure projects while managing the expectations of lenders, investors and key stakeholders?

We are looking for an experienced Senior Construction Project Manager to fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role across Elgin’s utility-scale solar PV, BESS and co-located PV/BESS projects. The role is focused on leading multidisciplinary project teams within a single Elgin delivery framework, ensuring that finance, legal, engineering, procurement, construction, operations, route-to-market and external adviser inputs are coordinated into one clear project position from late stage development / FID through construction, commissioning, commercial operations and handover to Asset Management. Particular emphasis will be placed on lender, investor, SPV governance and internal delivery interfaces.
 
This role requires significant project and contract management experience, including direct involvement in project finance processes, lender due diligence, conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender reporting, waivers / consents and coordination with lender technical advisers. The successful candidate will need specific experience with FIDIC based Construction Contracts, strong commercial judgement, disciplined contract administration capability and the ability to translate project delivery status into clear funding, governance and decision-making outputs.
 
To be successful in the role, you will have experience representing a client, employer, sponsor or SPV in the delivery of complex infrastructure or renewable energy projects. You will be commercially astute, highly organised, confident leading multidisciplinary project teams through a common governance and delivery framework, and capable of engaging credibly with lenders, investors, advisers, contractors, shareholder forums and senior internal stakeholders.

What you will be do:

  • Fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role for allocated projects, ensuring Elgin’s SPV, governance, commercial and contractual obligations are actively managed from FID through COD and handover.
  • Lead project and contract management on project-financed assets, coordinating lender processes including conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender technical adviser queries, lender reporting, waivers / consents and funding milestone submissions.
  • Administer and manage high-value EPC, ICP and related project contracts, including notices, variations, claims, payment applications, completion milestones, liquidated damages, defects and close-out obligations.
  • Maintain disciplined project controls across programme, budget, cash flow, risk, actions, decisions and change, ensuring transparent reporting to senior management, SPV governance bodies, lenders and investors.
  • Act as the primary project coordination point between Elgin’s internal project team, finance, legal, procurement, engineering, construction, operations, route-to-market and external advisers, ensuring that all workstreams operate from one integrated delivery plan, one risk position and one set of decision requirements.
  • Lead and manage multidisciplinary internal project teams within Elgin’s agreed delivery framework by setting priorities, clarifying accountabilities, managing dependencies, aligning workstreams to project milestones and escalating decisions in a timely and structured manner.
  • Manage the relationship and reporting cadence with project finance lenders, equity investors, shareholder representatives, lender technical advisers and other key finance-facing stakeholders, including preparing and presenting clear, decision-ready updates for shareholder forums and related governance meetings.
  • Oversee contractor, owner’s engineer and technical adviser interfaces to ensure delivery evidence, technical outputs and contractual positions support Elgin’s funding, governance and employer obligations.
  • Proactively identify commercial, contractual, programme and financing risks, develop mitigation plans and ensure issues are escalated with clear options, recommendations and decision requirements.
  • Support tendering, contract negotiation and commercial strategy by ensuring delivery arrangements are bankable, financeable, contractually robust and aligned with lender / investor expectations.


Your profile

What you will need: 

  • Degree in project management, construction management, engineering, or similar.
  • Extensive experience in infrastructure, renewables, power, energy storage or comparable capital projects, with significant project and contract management responsibility.
  • Direct experience working on project-financed projects, including lender due diligence, , funding drawdowns, lender technical adviser processes and ongoing lender / investor reporting.
  • Strong understanding of the Client / Employer’s Representative role and experience representing an owner, SPV, sponsor or employer in the delivery of complex contracted projects.

Our Mission

At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: procurement – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger 50+ emails, and pull in Finance, Legal, Security, and IT just to get something approved.

We’ve raised $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, and Accel to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.

The opportunity is massive. Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the 4th fastest growing startup in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.

Our team previously scaled Tessian (cybersecurity tech, backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel, acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone hungry to learn and early in their career to join us as our Revenue Operations Associate!

You'll get an inside look at, and be a key part of, how a high-performing GTM function operates: this is a great opportunity for exceptionally smart, motivated individuals who want to immerse themselves in the world of tech startups and gain real exposure to what it takes to keep a high-growth business moving.

You'll sit at the intersection of our GTM, Customer and Finance teams, keeping our systems, data, and reporting sharp as we scale. This isn't a "keep the lights on" role – you'll inherit processes that are still being built, and you'll have real room to audit what's working, fix what isn't, and put your own stamp on how we operate.

You'll get broad exposure early: one week you might be untangling a HubSpot workflow, the next you're building a dashboard the CCO takes into a board meeting. It's a genuinely excellent grounding in how a B2B SaaS business scales – but it comes with real pace, longer hours than a typical first job, and a learning curve to match. If you want breadth of exposure and a steep climb early in your career, this is a great seat.

What Can You Expect?

  • Keep our GTM tech stack in good shape: Own day-to-day CRM administration – data hygiene, permissions, and workflow upkeep – and support the configuration and integration of the wider stack.

  • Stay ahead of what's new: Keep across releases and new features across our tools – joining release webinars, reading release notes, and flagging what's worth adopting.

  • Help evaluate and set up new tools: Get involved as we add to the stack, from evaluation through to implementation.

  • Improve our data quality: Spot where data is incomplete or inconsistent, fix what you can, and propose fixes for the rest.

  • Build reporting and dashboards: Turn raw data into dashboards and reports that track pipeline health, funnel conversion, and the other KPIs the GTM team relies on day to day.

  • Support incentive tracking: Help maintain and monitor commission and incentive tracking, making sure calculations are accurate.

  • Onboard new GTM joiners: Train new starters across the GTM and Customer teams on our tools and processes so they're productive quickly.

  • Own our recurring admin cadence: Take ownership of the regular tasks that keep the engine running and look to automate where ever possible.

About You

  • You have a top-class academic record: you'll have graduated with (or be on track for) a 1st class degree, or have attended one of the top universities in the country you studied in – we're looking for a strong, proven track record of academic performance as the clearest early signal of the analytical rigour this role needs.

  • You're curious about how technology fits together: you likely have a STEM background, and you enjoy working out how systems, data, and workflows connect to make a business run – even if you've never worked in RevOps before.

  • You want pace, eyes open: you're drawn to a fast-scaling business precisely because of the pace, and you understand that means longer hours and a steeper learning curve than a typical grad role. You see that as a trade worth making.

  • You're happy to get stuck in: you know not every task here is glamorous – some of it is spreadsheet clean-up, data hygiene, or repetitive admin – and you take real satisfaction in doing that work well, not just the exciting parts.

  • You want to understand how B2B SaaS businesses scale: you're looking to build a first-hand understanding of the GTM engine – pipeline, systems, data, and the commercial mechanics behind it – as a foundation for wherever your career goes next.

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow!
